capital.zh: 特牧城（可能在巴普农附近）

summary.en: An early Indianised trading state of the lower Mekong, known chiefly from Chinese records. Its port of Óc Eo linked Indian Ocean and South China Sea commerce until Funan was eclipsed by Zhenla in the 6th century.
summary.zh: 湄公河下游早期受印度文化影响的贸易国家，主要见于中国史籍记载。其港口俄厄连接印度洋与南海贸易，6世纪被真腊取代。

name.zh: 阇耶跋摩（憍陈如阇耶跋摩）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Funan
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Michael Vickery, Society, Economics, and Politics in Pre-Angkor Cambodia (Centre for East Asian Cultural Studies, 1998)
Wikipedia: Funan

note: Founding and end dates are approximate (Wikidata gives 68–550); Fan Shiman's reign dates are estimates from Chinese accounts.

summary.en: A coastal civilisation of central and southern Vietnam made up of several Hindu–Buddhist Cham principalities that thrived on maritime trade. Gradually pushed south by Đại Việt, its last remnant was annexed by the Nguyễn in 1832.
summary.zh: 越南中南部沿海由多个信奉印度教与佛教的占族邦国组成的文明，以海上贸易兴盛。占婆逐渐被大越向南挤压，最后的残余于1832年被阮朝吞并。

name.zh: 阇耶僧伽跋摩三世（制旻）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Champa
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Champa

note: The 192 start follows the Chinese record of Lâm Ấp (Linyi); capitals shifted between Indrapura, Vijaya and Panduranga.

story.en:
The Cham were Austronesian seafarers whose kingdoms lined the narrow coastal plains of central and southern Vietnam for more than 1,400 years. Chinese records call the earliest Linyi, founded around 192 when a local official rebelled against Han rule. Cham kings wrote in Sanskrit and Cham, worshipped Shiva at the valley sanctuary of Mỹ Sơn and grew rich exporting eaglewood, cinnamon and ivory.

Champa was less a single state than a shifting league of principalities, Indrapura, Amaravati, Vijaya, Kauthara and Panduranga, each with its river port. It fought the Khmer for centuries, sacking Angkor in 1177, and the Vietnamese to the north. Under Chế Bồng Nga in the late 14th century Cham fleets sacked Thăng Long itself, but he was killed in 1390 and Champa never regained the initiative.

The fall of Vijaya in 1471 reduced it to the southern principality of Panduranga, which survived as a Vietnamese vassal until Emperor Minh Mạng abolished it in 1832. Some 160,000 Cham live in Vietnam today, and many more in Cambodia, where most are Muslim.
story.zh:
占人是南岛语系的航海民族，其王国沿越南中部和南部狭长的沿海平原分布了一千四百多年。中国史籍把最早的占人国家称为“林邑”，约192年由一名地方官吏反抗汉朝统治而建立。占婆国王使用梵文和占文，在美山谷地的圣地供奉湿婆，并靠出口沉香、肉桂和象牙致富。

与其说占婆是一个统一国家，不如说是一个不断变动的诸侯联盟，包括因陀罗补罗、阿摩罗缽底、毗阇耶、古笪罗和宾童龙，各有其河口港。它与高棉争战数百年，1177年曾攻陷吴哥，北方则与越南交锋。14世纪后期制蓬峨在位时，占婆舰队甚至攻掠了升龙，但他于1390年战死，此后占婆再也未能掌握主动。

1471年毗阇耶陷落后，占婆只剩南部的宾童龙，作为越南的藩属延续到1832年被明命帝废除。今天越南约有十六万占族人，柬埔寨的占族人更多，他们大多信奉伊斯兰教。

summary.en: A Buddhist maritime power centred on Palembang in Sumatra that controlled the Straits of Malacca and Sunda and was a centre of Buddhist learning visited by the Chinese pilgrim Yijing. Chola raids in 1025 weakened it.
summary.zh: 以苏门答腊巨港为中心的佛教海上强国，控制马六甲海峡与巽他海峡，也是佛学中心，唐代高僧义净曾在此求学。1025年朱罗王朝的袭击使其衰落。

name.zh: 达本达·希扬·室利·阇耶那沙
思离朱啰无尼佛麻调华
桑格拉玛·毗阇耶东伽跋摩

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Srivijaya
O. W. Wolters, Early Indonesian Commerce: A Study of the Origins of Śrīvijaya (Cornell University Press, 1967)
George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Wikipedia: Srivijaya

note: Dates are approximate; Wikidata gives 650–1377, and the later "Sanfoqi" of Chinese sources may refer to successor centres such as Jambi.

story.en:
Srivijaya was a kingdom of rivers and straits. From its centre near Palembang on the Musi river it controlled the Strait of Malacca and the Sunda Strait, through which ships carrying Chinese silk and Indian and Middle Eastern goods had to pass while waiting for the monsoons to turn. Its kings collected tolls, supplied ships with water and rice, and relied on the loyalty of the sea peoples, the Orang Laut, to police the waters.

Its history is pieced together from a handful of Old Malay inscriptions of the 680s, Chinese records of embassies, and travellers such as the monk Yijing, who praised its Buddhist scholarship. Arab geographers knew it as Zabag, ruled by a maharaja so rich that he threw a gold brick into a pond every day. Srivijayan kings endowed a Buddhist monastery at Nagapattinam in South India, but in 1025 the Chola emperor Rajendra I sent a fleet that sacked Srivijaya's ports and captured its king.

Srivijaya survived in weakened form, its centre shifting to Jambi, until Javanese expansion overwhelmed it in the 13th and 14th centuries. Its memory lived on in Parameswara, the Palembang prince who founded Malacca.
story.zh:
室利佛逝是一个属于河流与海峡的王国。它以穆西河畔巨港附近为中心，控制着马六甲海峡和巽他海峡；装载中国丝绸以及印度和中东货物的船只，必须在这里等候季风转向。国王们收取通行税，为船只供应淡水和稻米，并依靠“海人”（奥朗劳特）的效忠来维持海上秩序。

它的历史只能从7世纪80年代的几块古马来文碑铭、中国的朝贡记录，以及义净等旅行者的记载中拼凑出来；义净称赞了这里的佛学。阿拉伯地理学家称之为“扎巴格”，说其国王富有到每天往池塘里扔一块金砖。室利佛逝国王曾在南印度的那格伯蒂纳姆捐建佛寺，但1025年朱罗皇帝拉金德拉一世派舰队洗劫了室利佛逝的港口并俘虏了国王。

室利佛逝以衰弱的形态延续下来，中心转移到占碑，直到13至14世纪被爪哇的扩张所吞没。它的记忆延续在拜里米苏拉身上，这位巨港王子后来建立了马六甲。

summary.en: Founded when Jayavarman II proclaimed himself universal monarch on Phnom Kulen in 802, the Angkorian empire dominated mainland Southeast Asia, engineered vast reservoirs and built Angkor Wat and the Bayon.
summary.zh: 802年阇耶跋摩二世在荔枝山自立为“转轮王”，吴哥帝国由此建立。它称雄东南亚大陆，修建了庞大的水利系统以及吴哥窟、巴戎寺等建筑。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Angkor
Wikipedia: Khmer Empire

note: Both 802 and 1431 are conventional dates.

story.en:
For six centuries the Khmer kings ruled from the plain north of the Tonle Sap lake. Their power rested on water: huge rectangular reservoirs, the barays, and a web of canals that stored the monsoon rains, while each king proclaimed his legitimacy by building a temple-mountain at the centre of his city. Yasovarman I founded Yasodharapura around Phnom Bakheng about 900; Suryavarman II raised Angkor Wat; Jayavarman VII, after the Cham sack of 1177, built the walled city of Angkor Thom with the Bayon at its heart and a network of roads, rest houses and hospitals.

At its height the empire's influence reached from southern Vietnam to the Chao Phraya basin and into Laos. Lidar surveys since 2012 have shown that greater Angkor was a sprawling low-density city of perhaps 700,000 to 900,000 people.

The decline was gradual. Theravada Buddhism replaced the royal cults, trade shifted to the coast, Ayutthaya grew stronger, and tree rings suggest decades of severe drought and floods in the 14th and 15th centuries that strained the water system. After an Ayutthayan attack around 1431, the court moved south towards Phnom Penh.
story.zh:
六个世纪里，高棉国王们在洞里萨湖以北的平原上进行统治。他们的权力建立在水利之上：巨大的长方形水库（巴莱）和纵横交错的运河蓄积季风雨水；每位国王都在都城中央修建一座“神山”式寺庙，以昭示其统治的合法性。耶输跋摩一世约在900年以巴肯山为中心建立耶输陀罗补罗；苏利耶跋摩二世兴建吴哥窟；阇耶跋摩七世在1177年占城入侵之后，修筑了以巴戎寺为中心的吴哥通王城，以及道路、驿站和医院组成的网络。

鼎盛时期，帝国的影响从越南南部延伸到湄南河流域并深入老挝。2012年以来的激光雷达测绘显示，大吴哥地区是一座低密度蔓延的城市，人口可能达到七十万至九十万。

衰落是渐进的。上座部佛教取代了王室崇拜，贸易转向沿海，阿瑜陀耶日益强大；树木年轮显示，14至15世纪曾出现数十年的严重干旱与洪涝，使水利系统不堪重负。约1431年阿瑜陀耶进攻后，王廷南迁至金边一带。

summary.en: The first kingdom to unite the Irrawaddy valley, under Anawrahta from 1044. It spread Theravada Buddhism and the Burmese script, filled its capital with temples, and fragmented after the Mongol invasions of the 1280s.
summary.zh: 1044年阿奴律陀即位后首次统一伊洛瓦底江流域的王国。它传播上座部佛教与缅文，都城佛塔林立，13世纪80年代蒙古入侵后分裂瓦解。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Pagan Kingdom
Michael Aung-Thwin, Pagan: The Origins of Modern Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 1985)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Pagan Kingdom

note: The 849 founding is from the chronicles; the imperial phase begins in 1044.

summary.en: The first long-lived Vietnamese dynasty, which founded Thăng Long, named the state Đại Việt (1054), patronised Buddhism, set up the Temple of Literature (1070) and defeated a Song invasion in 1077.
summary.zh: 越南第一个长期统治的王朝。李朝建都升龙，1054年定国号大越，崇奉佛教，1070年兴建文庙，并于1077年击退宋军入侵。

sources.title: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Lý dynasty

summary.en: Successor to the Lý through a marriage engineered by Trần Thủ Độ, the Trần repelled three Mongol–Yuan invasions and fostered the Trúc Lâm school of Vietnamese Zen before being usurped by Hồ Quý Ly.
summary.zh: 经陈守度安排的联姻继承李朝的王朝。陈朝三次击退蒙元入侵，倡导越南禅宗竹林派，后被胡季犛篡夺。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Trần dynasty
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Trần dynasty

summary.en: Founded by Lê Lợi after expelling the Ming, it reached its height under Lê Thánh Tông, who conquered Vijaya in 1471 and issued the Hồng Đức code. Later the Lê emperors were figureheads under the Mạc, Trịnh and Nguyễn lords until the Tây Sơn ended the dynasty.
summary.zh: 黎利驱逐明军后建立的王朝，在黎圣宗时期臻于鼎盛：1471年攻取毗阇耶，颁布《洪德法典》。后期黎帝成为莫氏、郑主和阮主控制下的傀儡，最终被西山朝终结。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Later Lê dynasty
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: Later Lê dynasty early period

note: Interrupted by the Mạc dynasty (1527–1533/92); the restored Lê (1533–1789) were largely nominal rulers.

summary.en: A Hindu–Buddhist kingdom of East Java founded by Raden Wijaya after the Yuan invasion. Under Hayam Wuruk and Gajah Mada it claimed tribute from much of the archipelago, as celebrated in the Nāgarakṛtāgama, before declining amid the rise of Muslim coastal states.
summary.zh: 元军入侵后由罗登·威查耶在东爪哇建立的印度教—佛教王国。在哈奄·武禄与加查·马达治下，它向群岛大部分地区索取朝贡，《爪哇史颂》对此多有颂扬；后在沿海穆斯林国家兴起中衰落。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Majapahit
Mpu Prapañca, Deśawarṇana (Nāgarakṛtāgama, 1365), trans. Stuart Robson (KITLV, 1995)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Wikipedia: Majapahit

note: The end date (c. 1527, fall to Demak) is debated; the extent of its "empire" is likely overstated in court poetry.

story.en:
Majapahit was born from a double betrayal. In 1292 the Singhasari king Kertanegara was killed by a rebel from Kediri; his son-in-law Raden Wijaya feigned submission, opened land at Majapahit on the Brantas river, and when Kublai Khan's punitive fleet landed in 1293, used it to destroy the rebel before turning on the Mongols and driving them back to their ships.

Under Queen Tribhuwana and her son Hayam Wuruk, with the chief minister Gajah Mada, Majapahit became the greatest state of the archipelago. Prapanca's poem Nagarakretagama (1365) describes the capital at Trowulan, with brick walls, markets and Shaivite and Buddhist clergy, and lists nearly a hundred places from Sumatra to New Guinea said to acknowledge the king. Many were trading partners rather than subjects, but Javanese power was felt across the islands.

After Hayam Wuruk's death succession wars weakened the kingdom, and the rising Muslim ports of Java's north coast drew away its trade. Demak defeated it in the early 16th century. Indonesian nationalists later made Majapahit the model of a united archipelago, and its red-and-white banner inspired the national flag.
story.zh:
满者伯夷诞生于一场双重背叛。1292年，信诃沙里国王格尔达纳卡拉被谏义里叛臣杀害；他的女婿罗登·威查亚假意归顺，在布兰塔斯河畔的满者伯夷开垦土地。1293年忽必烈的问罪舰队登陆后，他借元军之力消灭叛臣，随即反戈一击，把元军赶回船上。

在特里布瓦纳女王和其子哈奄·武禄统治下，加上宰相加查·马达的辅佐，满者伯夷成为群岛中最强大的国家。普拉潘扎1365年的长诗《爪哇史颂》描绘了都城特罗武兰的砖墙、集市以及湿婆教和佛教僧侣，并列出从苏门答腊到新几内亚近百个据称臣服于国王的地方。其中许多其实是贸易伙伴而非属地，但爪哇的势力确实遍及群岛。

哈奄·武禄死后，王位争夺战削弱了王国，爪哇北岸新兴的穆斯林港口又夺走了它的贸易。16世纪初，满者伯夷被淡目击败。后来的印尼民族主义者把满者伯夷视为群岛统一的典范，其红白旗也成为国旗的灵感来源。

summary.en: An early Tai kingdom in the upper Chao Phraya basin, traditionally regarded as the first Thai state. Under Ram Khamhaeng it expanded and adopted Theravada Buddhism; it later became a vassal and then part of Ayutthaya.
summary.zh: 湄南河上游早期的泰族王国，传统上被视为第一个泰国国家。兰甘亨在位时向外扩张并奉行上座部佛教，后沦为阿瑜陀耶的藩属，最终被并入。

name.zh: 立泰王（摩诃昙摩罗阇一世）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sukhothai Kingdom
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Town of Sukhothai and Associated Historic Towns
Wikipedia: Sukhothai Kingdom

note: The 1238 founding is conventional; the authenticity of the Ram Khamhaeng inscription has been debated.

name.zh: 阿瑜陀耶王朝（大城王朝）

summary.en: A Siamese kingdom founded by U Thong on an island in the Chao Phraya. For four centuries it was one of Asia's great trading capitals, absorbing Sukhothai and sacking Angkor, until the Burmese destroyed it in 1767.
summary.zh: 乌通王在湄南河中的岛上建立的暹罗王国。四个世纪里它是亚洲重要的贸易都城之一，兼并素可泰并攻陷吴哥，1767年被缅军摧毁。

name.zh: 乌通王（拉玛铁菩提一世）

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Ayutthaya Kingdom
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Royal Chronicles of Ayutthaya, trans. Richard D. Cushman (Siam Society, 2000)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic City of Ayutthaya
Wikipedia: Ayutthaya Kingdom

note: Wikidata gives 1350; the traditional founding date is 1351.

story.en:
Ayutthaya sat on an island where three rivers met, about 80 km up the Chao Phraya from the sea, which made it both a rice-bowl capital and an ocean port. From its founding in 1351 it grew by absorbing Sukhothai and pushing back the Khmer, and by the 17th century it was one of the great cosmopolitan cities of Asia, with Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese, Dutch, Persian and Malay quarters around its walls.

Foreigners rose high at its court. A Japanese adventurer, Yamada Nagamasa, commanded the royal guard in the 1620s; a Greek, Constantine Phaulkon, became chief minister to King Narai and invited a French embassy and troops, until a palace revolution in 1688 executed him and closed the kingdom to French influence. European visitors compared the city to Venice for its canals and wrote of its hundreds of gilded temples.

Ayutthaya was sacked by Bayinnaung in 1569 and recovered under Naresuan. The second Burmese conquest, in 1767, was final: the city was burned and its people deported. The ruined brick stupas and Buddha heads entwined in tree roots are now among Thailand's most visited sites.
story.zh:
阿瑜陀耶坐落在三条河流交汇处的岛上，距入海口约80公里，既是稻米之乡的都城，又是远洋港口。1351年建城后，它吞并素可泰、击退高棉，逐步壮大；到17世纪已成为亚洲最国际化的大城市之一，城墙周围分布着中国、日本、葡萄牙、荷兰、波斯和马来人的聚居区。

外国人可以在宫廷中位极人臣。17世纪20年代，日本冒险家山田长政统领王家卫队；希腊人康斯坦丁·华尔康出任那莱王的首席大臣，并邀请法国使团和军队前来，直到1688年一场宫廷政变将他处死，暹罗从此关闭了对法国的大门。欧洲访客把这座运河纵横的城市比作威尼斯，并记述了城中数以百计的镀金寺庙。

1569年阿瑜陀耶被莽应龙攻破，在纳黎萱时期得以复兴。1767年缅军第二次攻陷它，则成为最后的结局：城市被焚毁，居民被掳走。如今那些残破的砖塔和被树根缠绕的佛头，是泰国游客最多的景点之一。

summary.en: A Malay maritime state that grew from Parameswara's settlement into the dominant entrepôt of the Straits. Its rulers adopted Islam, received Zheng He's fleets, and set the model of Malay kingship before the Portuguese conquest of 1511.
summary.zh: 由拜里米苏拉的聚落发展而来的马来海上国家，成为海峡地区首要的转口贸易港。其君主皈依伊斯兰教，接待郑和船队，奠定了马来王权的典范，1511年被葡萄牙征服。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Malacca Sultanate
Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals), trans. C. C. Brown (1952)
Tomé Pires, Suma Oriental (1512–1515), trans. Armando Cortesão (Hakluyt Society, 1944)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Malacca Sultanate

summary.en: Rising from the small principality of Toungoo, Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung reunited Burma and built a vast but short-lived empire. A restored Toungoo state ruled from Ava until Mon rebels sacked it in 1752.
summary.zh: 东吁王朝从小邦东吁崛起，莽瑞体与莽应龙重新统一缅甸，建立了庞大但短暂的帝国。复兴后的东吁王朝以阿瓦为都，直至1752年被孟族起义军攻破。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Toungoo dynasty
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Hmannan Yazawin (Glass Palace Chronicle, 1832)
Wikipedia: Toungoo dynasty

note: Start date disputed: Wikidata and Britannica date the dynasty from Mingyinyo's accession at Toungoo (1485/86; Britannica also allows 1531, Tabinshwehti's accession); 1510 marks Toungoo's break with Ava.

capital.zh: 曼德勒（1857年起）；此前为阿瓦、阿摩罗补罗

summary.en: Founded by Alaungpaya, the last Burmese dynasty destroyed Ayutthaya, repelled Qing invasions and expanded into Arakan, Manipur and Assam, before losing three wars to Britain; Thibaw was deposed in 1885.
summary.zh: 由雍籍牙建立的缅甸末代王朝。它摧毁阿瑜陀耶、击退清军入侵，并向若开、曼尼普尔与阿萨姆扩张，后在三次英缅战争中战败，1885年锡袍王被废黜。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Konbaung dynasty
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, Vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Wikipedia: Konbaung dynasty

name.zh: 拉达那哥欣王朝（暹罗曼谷王朝）

summary.en: The Chakri kingdom founded by Rama I at Bangkok. Mongkut and Chulalongkorn modernised the state and ceded border territories, keeping Siam the only Southeast Asian country never colonised, until the 1932 revolution ended absolute monarchy.
summary.zh: 拉玛一世在曼谷建立的却克里王朝。蒙固王与朱拉隆功推行现代化改革并割让部分边地，使暹罗成为东南亚唯一未被殖民的国家，直至1932年革命结束君主专制。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Rattanakosin Kingdom (1782–1932)

note: Prajadhipok reigned until 1935; his entry is truncated at the end of absolute monarchy.

summary.en: Founded by Gia Long after defeating the Tây Sơn, it ruled a unified Vietnam from Huế and named the country Việt Nam. France conquered it between 1858 and 1885, after which the emperors reigned under French protection until Bảo Đại abdicated in 1945.
summary.zh: 嘉隆帝击败西山朝后建立的王朝，以顺化为都统治统一的越南，并定国号“越南”。1858至1885年间被法国征服，此后皇帝在法国保护下名义在位，直至1945年保大帝退位。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica: Nguyễn dynasty
Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Complex of Hué Monuments
Wikipedia: Nguyễn dynasty

capital.zh: 哥打格德，后迁卡尔塔苏拉

summary.en: The last great Javanese kingdom before Dutch dominance. Sultan Agung conquered most of Java and twice besieged Batavia (1628–29); later succession wars drew in the VOC, and the 1755 Treaty of Giyanti split it into Yogyakarta and Surakarta.
summary.zh: 荷兰称霸前爪哇最后一个强大王国。苏丹阿贡征服爪哇大部，并两度围攻巴达维亚（1628—1629年）；此后的王位继承战争引来荷兰东印度公司介入，1755年《吉扬蒂条约》将其分裂为日惹与梭罗。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (Palgrave, 4th ed. 2008)
Nicholas Tarling (ed.), The Cambridge History of Southeast Asia, Vol. 1: From Early Times to c. 1800 (1992)
Wikipedia: Mataram Sultanate

summary.en: Walled, moated brick cities of the Tibeto-Burman-speaking Pyu in the Irrawaddy valley (Beikthano, Halin, Sri Ksetra), early centres of Buddhism and rice irrigation in Burma. Chinese sources call the realm Piao; Nanzhao raids in the 830s ended its independence.
summary.zh: 藏缅语族骠人在伊洛瓦底江流域建立的砖砌城邦（毗湿奴城、汉林、室利差呾罗），城有城墙与护城河，是缅甸早期佛教和水稻灌溉的中心。汉文史料称之为“骠国”，9世纪30年代南诏的劫掠终结了其独立。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Pyu Ancient Cities
Janice Stargardt, The Ancient Pyu of Burma (Cambridge, 1990)
G. H. Luce, Phases of Pre-Pagan Burma (Oxford University Press, 1985)
Wikipedia: Pyu city-states

note: Start and end are archaeological estimates. The three Vikrama kings are known from inscribed funerary urns at Sri Ksetra; the years usually read from them (688, 695, 718) and even the kings' order have been disputed since another urn was found in 1993, so the reign dates are approximate.

story.en:
Long before Pagan, the dry zone of central Burma was a land of round brick cities. Beikthano, Halin and Sri Ksetra each enclosed palaces, monasteries, fields and reservoirs inside walls several kilometres around, and their people, the Pyu, cremated their dead and buried the ashes in inscribed urns. Gold leaf manuscripts of Pali scripture from Sri Ksetra are among the oldest Buddhist texts in Southeast Asia.

The Tang court knew them as Piao. In 802 a Pyu embassy reached Chang'an with a troupe of musicians and dancers, and the poet Bai Juyi wrote a ballad about their performance. Thirty years later the Pyu world collapsed: the Manshu, a Tang account of Nanzhao, records that Nanzhao armies sacked a Pyu city in 832 and carried off some three thousand captives to Yunnan.

The Burmans who founded Pagan inherited Pyu irrigation, script and Buddhist practice. In 2014 the three cities became Myanmar's first World Heritage site.
story.zh:
早在蒲甘之前，缅甸中部干旱区就分布着一座座圆形的砖城。毗湿奴城、汉林和室利差呾罗的城墙周长达数公里，城内有宫殿、寺院、田地和水库。城中居民骠人实行火葬，把骨灰葬入刻有铭文的瓮中。室利差呾罗出土的金叶巴利文佛经，是东南亚最古老的佛教文献之一。

唐朝称之为“骠国”。802年，骠国使团携乐工舞伎抵达长安，白居易为此写下《骠国乐》。三十年后骠人世界崩溃：唐人记述南诏的《蛮书》记载，832年南诏军攻破骠国城邑，掳走约三千人迁往云南。

建立蒲甘的缅人继承了骠人的灌溉、文字与佛教传统。2014年，这三座古城成为缅甸第一处世界遗产。

capital.zh: 伊奢那补罗（三波坡雷古）

summary.en: Khmer kingdom of the middle Mekong that absorbed Funan in the 6th–7th centuries. Its kings built the brick temple city of Isanapura; after about 706 Chinese sources speak of a divided "Land" and "Water" Chenla until Jayavarman II reunited the Khmer in 802.
summary.zh: 湄公河中游的高棉王国，6至7世纪吞并扶南。其国王修建了砖砌神庙之城伊奢那补罗；约706年后，汉文史料称其分裂为“陆真腊”和“水真腊”，直到802年阇耶跋摩二世重新统一高棉。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Michael Vickery, Society, Economics, and Politics in Pre-Angkor Cambodia (Toyo Bunko, 1998)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Temple Zone of Sambor Prei Kuk
Wikipedia: Chenla

note: Wikidata ends Chenla at 706 (the split into Land and Water Chenla); here the divided period runs on to 802 so the Khmer succession has no gap. Reigns are approximate.

summary.en: A Mon Buddhist culture of moated cities in the Chao Phraya basin, named from silver coins inscribed "merit of the lord of Dvaravati". Its Theravada art and city plans shaped later Thai kingdoms before Angkor absorbed much of it in the 11th century.
summary.zh: 湄南河流域孟人的佛教文化，城镇环以护城河，得名于刻有“堕罗钵底之主的功德”字样的银币。其上座部佛教艺术与城市布局影响了后来的泰人王国，11世纪大部分地区被吴哥吞并。

sources.title: Robert L. Brown, The Dvāravatī Wheels of the Law and the Indianization of South East Asia (Brill, 1996)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Wikipedia: Dvaravati

note: Dvaravati may have been a cultural sphere of several principalities rather than one state; no ruler list survives.

capital.en: Mdang i Bhumi Mataram (Central Java); East Java after 929
capital.zh: 马打兰地区的梅当（中爪哇）；929年后迁东爪哇

summary.en: The Hindu-Buddhist kingdom of Central Java whose Sailendra and Sanjaya lines raised Borobudur and Prambanan. Around 929 Mpu Sindok moved the court to East Java, perhaps after an eruption of Merapi; the realm fell in 1016 when Wurawari, allied with Srivijaya, sacked the capital.
summary.zh: 中爪哇的印度教—佛教王国，夏连特拉与珊阇耶两系在此修建了婆罗浮屠和普兰巴南。约929年，辛多克（Mpu Sindok）将王廷迁往东爪哇，可能与默拉皮火山喷发有关；1016年与室利佛逝结盟的乌拉瓦里攻破都城，王国覆亡。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Paul Michel Munoz, Early Kingdoms of the Indonesian Archipelago and the Malay Peninsula (Editions Didier Millet, 2006)
Jan Wisseman Christie, "Revisiting early Mataram", in Fruits of Inspiration (Forsten, 2001)
Wikipedia: Mataram Kingdom

note: Whether the Sailendras and the Sanjaya line were rival dynasties or one house is debated; reigns are approximate from inscriptions.

summary.en: The East Javanese kingdom rebuilt by Airlangga after the fall of Medang in 1016. Before retiring as a hermit he divided it between two sons into Janggala and Panjalu (Kediri), which the Old Javanese tradition remembers as the partition of Java.
summary.zh: 1016年梅当覆亡后，爱尔棱伽在东爪哇重建的王国。他出家隐修前将国土分给两个儿子，形成章加拉与班查卢（谏义里），古爪哇传统称之为“爪哇分治”。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Paul Michel Munoz, Early Kingdoms of the Indonesian Archipelago and the Malay Peninsula (Editions Didier Millet, 2006)
Wikipedia: Kahuripan

note: Airlangga's abdication and the partition are dated c. 1042–1045.

summary.en: East Javanese kingdom on the Brantas river that dominated the spice trade to Maluku and produced the golden age of Old Javanese kakawin poetry, including the Bharatayuddha. Ken Arok of Tumapel overthrew its last king, Kertajaya, at Ganter in 1222.
summary.zh: 布兰塔斯河畔的东爪哇王国，控制通往马鲁古的香料贸易，古爪哇语“格卡温”诗歌在此进入黄金时代，《婆罗多大战》即成书于此。1222年，杜马板的肯·阿洛在甘特尔击败末代国王格尔塔查亚。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Paul Michel Munoz, Early Kingdoms of the Indonesian Archipelago and the Malay Peninsula (Editions Didier Millet, 2006)
Zhao Rugua, Zhufan zhi (Description of Foreign Peoples, 1225)
Wikipedia: Kediri Kingdom

note: Wikidata gives 1045–1221; the Battle of Ganter is traditionally 1222 (Pararaton).

summary.en: East Javanese kingdom founded by the adventurer Ken Arok. Its last king, Kertanegara, sent the Pamalayu expedition to Sumatra and defied Kublai Khan, but was killed by the rebel Jayakatwang in 1292, setting the stage for Majapahit.
summary.zh: 冒险家肯·阿洛建立的东爪哇王国。末代国王格尔达纳卡拉派出“征末罗瑜”远征苏门答腊，并公然对抗忽必烈，1292年被叛臣查亚卡特望所杀，为满者伯夷的兴起铺平了道路。

sources.title: George Cœdès, The Indianized States of Southeast Asia (University of Hawaii Press, 1968)
Paul Michel Munoz, Early Kingdoms of the Indonesian Archipelago and the Malay Peninsula (Editions Didier Millet, 2006)
Pararaton (Book of Kings), Old Javanese chronicle
Prapanca, Nagarakretagama (1365)
Wikipedia: Singhasari

note: The Pararaton's tale of Ken Arok and the cursed kris is legend; reigns follow the Nagarakretagama.

story.en:
According to the Pararaton, Singhasari began with a curse. Ken Arok, a robber of low birth, ordered a kris from the smith Mpu Gandring, grew impatient and stabbed him with the unfinished blade. Dying, the smith foretold that the dagger would kill seven kings. Ken Arok used it to murder the regent of Tumapel, married his widow Ken Dedes, and in 1222 defeated Kertajaya of Kediri at Ganter. The chronicle says the kris then passed from hand to hand through a string of royal murders.

The kingdom's last ruler, Kertanegara, was more than a court intriguer. He sent the Pamalayu expedition of 1275 to win influence in Sumatra, practised a Tantric Buddhism that fused with Shiva worship, and in 1289 sent Kublai Khan's envoy Meng Qi home with his face branded.

In 1292 a Kediri prince, Jayakatwang, rose and killed Kertanegara. When the Mongol fleet arrived to punish the insult, Kertanegara's son-in-law Raden Wijaya turned it against Jayakatwang and then drove the Mongols out, founding Majapahit.
story.zh:
据《诸王志》（Pararaton）记载，信诃沙里起源于一个诅咒。出身低微的强盗肯·阿洛向铸剑师甘德凌订制一把格里斯短剑，等得不耐烦，便用未完工的剑刺死了他。铸剑师临死前预言此剑将杀死七位国王。肯·阿洛用它刺杀了杜马板的摄政，娶其遗孀肯·德德斯，1222年又在甘特尔击败谏义里国王格尔塔查亚。据编年史说，这把剑此后在一连串王室谋杀中辗转易手。

末代国王格尔达纳卡拉并非只会宫廷权谋。1275年他派出“征末罗瑜”远征扩大在苏门答腊的影响，信奉与湿婆崇拜融合的密宗佛教；1289年，他在忽必烈使者孟琪脸上刺字后将其遣回。

1292年，谏义里王子查亚卡特望起兵杀死格尔达纳卡拉。元军舰队前来问罪时，格尔达纳卡拉的女婿罗登·威查亚借元军之力消灭查亚卡特望，随即又把元军赶走，建立了满者伯夷。

summary.en: "Kingdom of a million rice fields", the Tai kingdom of northern Thailand founded by Mangrai. A centre of Theravada learning under Tilokarat, it fell to Bayinnaung in 1558 and stayed a Burmese dependency until Chiang Mai went over to Siam in 1774–1775.
summary.zh: “百万稻田之国”，孟莱王在泰北建立的泰人王国。提洛卡拉王时期是上座部佛教学术中心，1558年被莽应龙征服，此后长期附属缅甸，直到1774—1775年清迈归附暹罗。

sources.title: David K. Wyatt & Aroonrut Wichienkeeo (trans.), The Chiang Mai Chronicle (Silkworm Books, 2nd ed. 1998)
Hans Penth, A Brief History of Lan Na (Silkworm Books, 1994)
Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
Wikipedia: Lan Na

note: Mangrai ruled Ngoenyang from 1261; 1292 marks his conquest of Haripunchai. From 1558 to 1775 Lan Na was mostly under Burmese rule.

capital.en: Xieng Dong Xieng Thong (Luang Prabang); Vientiane from 1560
capital.zh: 川铜（琅勃拉邦）；1560年起万象

summary.en: The "kingdom of a million elephants", founded by Fa Ngum in 1353 and the ancestor of Laos. Setthathirath moved the capital to Vientiane and built That Luang; after Sourigna Vongsa's long reign a succession dispute split it into Luang Prabang, Vientiane and Champasak.
summary.zh: “万象之国”，1353年由法昂建立，是老挝的前身。塞塔提拉王迁都万象并修建塔銮；苏里亚旺萨长期统治之后，王位之争使其在1707年后分裂为琅勃拉邦、万象和占巴塞三国。

sources.title: Martin Stuart-Fox, The Lao Kingdom of Lān Xāng: Rise and Decline (White Lotus, 1998)
Martin Stuart-Fox, A History of Laos (Cambridge University Press, 1997)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Laos: History
Wikipedia: Lan Xang

note: Founding is traditionally 1353 (Wikidata 1354); the formal split came in 1707.

story.en:
The Lao chronicles open Lan Xang's history with an exile. Fa Ngum, a prince of Muang Sua (Luang Prabang) whose family had been banished, grew up at the Khmer court at Angkor and married a Khmer princess. With an army lent by his father-in-law he marched up the Mekong, and in 1353 had himself crowned at Xieng Dong Xieng Thong as lord of the "million elephants".

The chronicles credit his Khmer queen with bringing Theravada monks and the Phra Bang, the golden Buddha image that later gave Luang Prabang its name. Fa Ngum himself proved a harsh ruler; in 1373 his nobles deposed him and he died in exile in Nan.

Lan Xang flourished for three centuries. Setthathirath, who had briefly ruled Lan Na as well, moved the capital to Vientiane in 1560 to escape Burmese pressure and raised the great stupa of That Luang. Dutch merchant Gerrit van Wuysthoff, who visited in 1641, was dazzled by its temples. After Sourigna Vongsa died without an undisputed heir, the kingdom broke apart in 1707.
story.zh:
老挝编年史以一段流亡开启澜沧的历史。法昂是孟骚（琅勃拉邦）的王子，因家族被放逐，在吴哥的高棉宫廷长大，并娶高棉公主为妻。他率岳父借给他的军队沿湄公河北上，1353年在川铜加冕，号称“百万大象”之主。

编年史称，是他的高棉王后带来了上座部僧侣和勃拉邦金佛，琅勃拉邦后来便因此佛得名。法昂本人统治严苛，1373年被贵族废黜，最终客死难府。

澜沧此后繁荣了三个世纪。曾一度兼领兰纳的塞塔提拉王为躲避缅甸压力，于1560年迁都万象，并兴建了宏伟的塔銮。1641年来访的荷兰商人范伍斯特霍夫为当地寺庙的华美所倾倒。苏里亚旺萨去世时没有无可争议的继承人，王国于1707年分裂。

summary.en: The southern-central successor of Lan Xang, a Siamese vassal from 1779. Its last king, Anouvong, rose against Bangkok in 1826–1828; Siamese armies razed Vientiane and deported much of its population to the Khorat plateau.
summary.zh: 澜沧分裂后形成的中南部王国，1779年起成为暹罗属国。末代国王阿努冯于1826—1828年起兵反抗曼谷，暹罗军队将万象夷为平地，并把大量居民迁往呵叻高原。

sources.title: Martin Stuart-Fox, A History of Laos (Cambridge University Press, 1997)
Mayoury & Pheuiphanh Ngaosrivathana, Paths to Conflagration: Fifty Years of Diplomacy and Warfare in Laos, Thailand, and Vietnam, 1778–1828 (Cornell SEAP, 1998)
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Vientiane

summary.en: The Mon kingdom of Lower Burma founded by Wareru after Pagan's collapse. Rich from the Bay of Bengal trade, it fought the Forty Years' War against Ava under Razadarit and flourished under Queen Shin Sawbu and Dhammazedi, before Toungoo conquered it in 1538–1539.
summary.zh: 蒲甘崩溃后瓦里鲁在下缅甸建立的孟人王国。依靠孟加拉湾贸易致富，罗娑陀利王时期与阿瓦进行了“四十年战争”，信修浮女王和达摩悉提王时期臻于繁荣，1538—1539年被东吁征服。

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
Michael Aung-Thwin, The Mists of Rāmañña: The Legend that was Lower Burma (University of Hawaii Press, 2005)
Wikipedia: Hanthawaddy kingdom

note: Toungoo took Pegu in 1539; a brief Mon restoration lasted 1550–1552.

summary.en: The dominant Burman kingdom of Upper Burma after Pagan, founded by Thado Minbya at the Irrawaddy–Myitnge confluence. It waged the Forty Years' War with Hanthawaddy and patronised Burmese literature, until Shan confederations and finally Bayinnaung overran it.
summary.zh: 蒲甘之后上缅甸最强大的缅人王国，由他拖弥婆耶建于伊洛瓦底江与密埃河交汇处。它与勃固进行了“四十年战争”，并扶持缅文文学，后来先后被掸族联盟和莽应龙攻灭。

sources.title: Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Thant Myint-U, The River of Lost Footsteps: Histories of Burma (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2006)
G. E. Harvey, History of Burma (Longmans, 1925)
Wikipedia: Ava Kingdom

summary.en: Coastal kingdom of Arakan founded by Min Saw Mon with help from the Sultanate of Bengal; its Buddhist kings used Islamic titles and minted coins in Persian. With Portuguese mercenaries it raided Bengal and once held Chittagong, until Bodawpaya's Burmese armies annexed it in 1784–1785.
summary.zh: 阿拉干沿海王国，明苏蒙在孟加拉苏丹国协助下建立；其佛教君主兼用伊斯兰称号，并铸造波斯文钱币。王国曾借助葡萄牙雇佣兵劫掠孟加拉、一度控制吉大港，1784—1785年被孟云的缅军吞并。

sources.title: Michael W. Charney, "Arakan, Min Yazagyi, and the Portuguese" (SOAS Bulletin of Burma Research, 2005)
Victor Lieberman, Strange Parallels: Southeast Asia in Global Context, c. 800–1830, vol. 1 (Cambridge University Press, 2003)
Wikipedia: Kingdom of Mrauk U

summary.en: The kingdom of Vạn Xuân ("Ten Thousand Springs") proclaimed by Lý Bí after he expelled the Liang governor of Jiaozhou. It was the first lasting Vietnamese bid for independence between the Trưng sisters and Ngô Quyền, and ended when the Sui reconquered the delta in 602.
summary.zh: 李贲驱逐梁朝交州刺史后建立的“万春国”，是二征起义与吴权之间越南最持久的一次独立尝试，602年隋朝重新征服红河三角洲后灭亡。

name.en: Hậu Lý Nam Đế (Lý Phật Tử)

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Keith W. Taylor, The Birth of Vietnam (University of California Press, 1983)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Early Lý dynasty

note: Triệu Việt Vương and Lý Phật Tử ruled rival halves for part of the period; Chinese histories treat all three as rebels.

summary.en: The first independent Vietnamese monarchy after a thousand years of Chinese rule, founded by Ngô Quyền after his victory at Bạch Đằng in 938. After his death in 944 it was usurped and then crumbled into the anarchy of the Twelve Warlords.
summary.zh: 吴权在938年白藤江大捷后建立，是越南结束千年北属后的第一个独立王朝。944年吴权死后王位被篡，随后陷入“十二使君”割据的混乱。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Ngô dynasty

summary.en: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh defeated the Twelve Warlords, took the title emperor and named the state Đại Cồ Việt, ruling from a limestone fortress at Hoa Lư. His assassination in 979 left a child on the throne and opened the way for Lê Hoàn.
summary.zh: 丁部领平定“十二使君”，称帝并定国号为“大瞿越”，以华闾的石灰岩要塞为都。979年他遇刺身亡，幼子继位，为黎桓上台打开了大门。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Đinh dynasty

summary.en: Founded by the general Lê Hoàn, who took the throne in 980 and in 981 repelled a Song invasion at Chi Lăng and Bạch Đằng, then sacked the Cham capital in 982. Under his cruel son Lê Long Đĩnh the dynasty collapsed and the court chose Lý Công Uẩn.
summary.zh: 由大将黎桓建立。他于980年即位，981年在支棱、白藤江击退宋军入侵，982年又攻破占城都城。其子黎龙铤残暴无道，王朝崩溃，朝臣拥立李公蕴。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Early Lê dynasty

summary.en: Hồ Quý Ly, a Trần regent, seized the throne in 1400, renamed the country Đại Ngu and pushed radical reforms: paper money, land limits and Vietnamese-script examinations. The Ming used his usurpation as a pretext to invade in 1406–1407 and annex the country.
summary.zh: 陈朝权臣胡季犛于1400年篡位，改国号为“大虞”，推行纸币、限田和以喃字取士等激进改革。明朝以其篡位为借口，于1406—1407年出兵并吞了越南。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
John K. Whitmore, Vietnam, Hồ Quý Ly, and the Ming (1371–1421) (Yale Southeast Asia Studies, 1985)
UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Citadel of the Ho Dynasty
Wikipedia: Hồ dynasty

summary.en: Mạc Đăng Dung, a Lê general, usurped the throne in 1527 and won Ming acceptance by ceding border districts. Lê loyalists backed by the Nguyễn and Trịnh clans fought him for sixty years; they retook Thăng Long in 1592, and the Mạc held out in Cao Bằng until 1677.
summary.zh: 后黎朝将领莫登庸于1527年篡位，以割让边地换取明朝承认。阮氏、郑氏扶持的黎朝复辟势力与莫朝交战六十年，1592年收复升龙，莫氏退守高平直到1677年。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư (Complete Annals of Đại Việt, 1479; 1697 ed.)
Wikipedia: Mạc dynasty

note: Main rule over the Red River delta was 1527–1592; Wikidata ends the dynasty in 1677 with the fall of Cao Bằng.

capital.en: Quy Nhơn (Hoàng Đế citadel); Phú Xuân (Huế)

summary.en: The regime of three brothers from Tây Sơn village who led a peasant rising in 1771, destroyed both the Nguyễn and Trịnh lords and the Lê dynasty, and beat Siamese and Qing invasions. Divided among the brothers and weakened by Quang Trung's early death, it fell to Nguyễn Ánh in 1802.
summary.zh: 来自西山邑的三兄弟所建立的政权。他们于1771年发动农民起义，先后消灭阮主、郑主和后黎朝，并击败暹罗与清军的入侵。兄弟分治，加之光中帝早逝，1802年被阮福映所灭。

sources.title: Keith W. Taylor, A History of the Vietnamese (Cambridge University Press, 2013)
George Dutton, The Tây Sơn Uprising: Society and Rebellion in Eighteenth-Century Vietnam (University of Hawaii Press, 2006)
Wikipedia: Tây Sơn dynasty

summary.en: The short-lived kingdom of Taksin, who rallied resistance after the Burmese sack of Ayutthaya, made Thonburi his capital and reunified Siam within a few years. He was deposed and executed in 1782, and his general Chao Phraya Chakri founded the Chakri dynasty across the river in Bangkok.
summary.zh: 郑信在缅军攻陷阿瑜陀耶后组织抵抗，以吞武里为都，数年内重新统一暹罗。1782年郑信被废黜处死，其大将昭披耶却克里在河对岸的曼谷建立却克里王朝。

sources.title: Chris Baker & Pasuk Phongpaichit, A History of Thailand (Cambridge University Press, 2nd ed. 2009)
David K. Wyatt, Thailand: A Short History (Yale University Press, 2nd ed. 2003)
Wikipedia: Thonburi Kingdom

note: Taksin was crowned at the end of 1767 (Wikidata gives 1768).

summary.en: After abandoning Angkor the Khmer court moved to the Mekong–Tonle Sap junction, trading with China, Japan and Europe from Longvek and later Oudong. Squeezed between Siam and Vietnam, it lost Longvek to Ayutthaya in 1594 and the Mekong delta to Vietnamese settlers, until King Norodom accepted a French protectorate in 1863.
summary.zh: 放弃吴哥后，高棉王廷迁到湄公河与洞里萨河交汇处，先后以洛韦、乌栋为都，与中国、日本和欧洲通商。王国夹在暹罗与越南之间，1594年洛韦被阿瑜陀耶攻陷，湄公河三角洲则逐渐被越南移民占据，直到1863年诺罗敦国王接受法国保护。

sources.title: David Chandler, A History of Cambodia (Westview, 4th ed. 2008)
Michael Vickery, Cambodia after Angkor: The Chronicular Evidence for the Fourteenth to Sixteenth Centuries (PhD thesis, Yale, 1977)
Wikipedia: Post-Angkor period

note: Royal chronicle dates for the 15th–16th centuries are uncertain; Ang Duong was regent from 1841 and crowned in 1848.

summary.en: Clove-growing island sultanate of North Maluku, Islamic from the late 15th century. Sultan Baabullah expelled the Portuguese in 1575 and briefly ruled a maritime empire across eastern Indonesia; later sultans became VOC vassals.
summary.zh: 北马鲁古出产丁香的海岛苏丹国，15世纪末皈依伊斯兰教。1575年巴布拉苏丹驱逐葡萄牙人，一度统治横跨印尼东部的海上帝国；后来的苏丹沦为荷兰东印度公司的附庸。

sources.title: Leonard Y. Andaya, The World of Maluku: Eastern Indonesia in the Early Modern Period (University of Hawaii Press, 1993)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Sultanate of Ternate

note: The 1257 founding is traditional; after 1683 the sultanate was a Dutch vassal, and it lost its last powers in 1946.

summary.en: The "Veranda of Mecca" at the northern tip of Sumatra, which grew rich on pepper after the Portuguese took Malacca and allied with the Ottomans against them. It peaked under Iskandar Muda, was ruled by four successive queens in 1641–1699, and resisted the Dutch for thirty years from 1873.
summary.zh: 位于苏门答腊北端的“麦加走廊”。葡萄牙人占领马六甲后，亚齐凭胡椒贸易致富，并与奥斯曼帝国结盟对抗葡萄牙。伊斯坎达·慕达时期达到鼎盛，1641—1699年由四位女苏丹相继统治，1873年起抵抗荷兰长达三十年。

name.zh: 塔朱·阿拉姆·萨菲亚图丁
穆罕默德·达乌德·沙二世

sources.title: Anthony Reid, An Indonesian Frontier: Acehnese and Other Histories of Sumatra (NUS Press, 2005)
M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Wikipedia: Aceh Sultanate

capital.zh: 哥打巴都 / 斯里巴加湾

summary.en: Malay sultanate on Borneo's north coast whose influence under Sultan Bolkiah reached Sulu and Manila. Spain attacked it in the Castilian War of 1578; over the 19th century it lost Sarawak and Sabah, and in 1888 became a British protectorate.
summary.zh: 婆罗洲北岸的马来苏丹国，博尔基亚苏丹时期势力远及苏禄和马尼拉。1578年西班牙在“卡斯蒂利亚战争”中进攻文莱；19世纪它先后失去砂拉越与沙巴，1888年成为英国保护国。

sources.title: Graham Saunders, A History of Brunei (Routledge, 2nd ed. 2002)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Bruneian Empire

note: Early dates follow Brunei's royal genealogy (Salasilah Raja-Raja Brunei).

name.en: Dutch East India Company rule in the Indies
name.zh: 荷兰东印度公司统治下的东印度

summary.en: The territorial empire of the VOC, run by a governor-general in Batavia from 1619. Through monopolies, force and alliances it controlled the spice islands, Java's north coast and Malacca; bankrupt and corrupt, the company was dissolved and its possessions passed to the Dutch state on 1 January 1800.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司的领土帝国，1619年起由驻巴达维亚的总督治理。公司凭借垄断、武力与结盟控制了香料群岛、爪哇北岸和马六甲；因破产与腐败，公司于1800年1月1日解散，属地移交荷兰国家。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Femme S. Gaastra, The Dutch East India Company: Expansion and Decline (Walburg Pers, 2003)
Wikipedia: Company rule in the Dutch East Indies

note: Rulers listed are governors-general; Coen held the office twice (1619–1623, 1627–1629).

summary.en: The Dutch state colony that succeeded the VOC and, through the Java War, the Cultivation System and the Aceh War, was extended over the whole archipelago by about 1910. Japan occupied it in 1942; after the Indonesian revolution the Netherlands transferred sovereignty in December 1949.
summary.zh: 继荷兰东印度公司之后由荷兰国家直接统治的殖民地。经过爪哇战争、强迫种植制度和亚齐战争，到约1910年统治扩及整个群岛。1942年被日本占领；印尼独立战争后，荷兰于1949年12月移交主权。

sources.title: M. C. Ricklefs, A History of Modern Indonesia since c. 1200 (4th ed., Stanford University Press, 2008)
Robert Cribb & Audrey Kahin, Historical Dictionary of Indonesia (Scarecrow, 2004)
Wikipedia: Dutch East Indies

note: British rule interrupted Dutch control of Java in 1811–1816; rulers listed are governors-general.

name.zh: 西属菲律宾（菲律宾都督府）

summary.en: Spain's Asian colony, governed from Manila under New Spain until 1821 and then directly from Madrid. Friars spread Catholicism across the lowlands, the Manila galleons linked it to Acapulco, and Muslim sultanates in the south resisted for three centuries until the 1896 revolution and the American war ended Spanish rule.
summary.zh: 西班牙在亚洲的殖民地，1821年前隶属新西班牙，之后由马德里直接管辖。修士们把天主教传遍低地，马尼拉大帆船将其与阿卡普尔科相连；南部穆斯林苏丹国抵抗长达三个世纪，直到1896年革命和美西战争终结了西班牙统治。

name.zh: 米格尔·洛佩斯·德黎牙实比
戈麦斯·佩雷斯·达斯马里尼亚斯

John Leddy Phelan, The Hispanization of the Philippines (University of Wisconsin Press, 1959)
Wikipedia: Captaincy General of the Philippines

note: Britain occupied Manila in 1762–1764 during the Seven Years' War.

summary.en: British colony uniting Penang, Malacca and Singapore, run by the East India Company until 1867 and then as a crown colony. Its free ports, Chinese and Indian merchants and tin and rubber trade made Singapore the hub of British Malaya; it was dissolved in 1946.
summary.zh: 由槟城、马六甲和新加坡组成的英国殖民地，1867年前归东印度公司管辖，之后成为直辖殖民地。自由港政策、华商与印商以及锡和橡胶贸易使新加坡成为英属马来亚的枢纽。1946年解散。

sources.title: C. M. Turnbull, A History of Modern Singapore 1819–2005 (NUS Press, 2009)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Straits Settlements

note: Rulers listed are governors; Japan occupied the colony 1942–1945.

summary.en: The private kingdom of the Brooke family, the "White Rajahs". James Brooke received Sarawak from the Sultan of Brunei in 1841 for helping crush a revolt; his successors expanded it at Brunei's expense until Vyner Brooke ceded it to the British crown in 1946.
summary.zh: 布鲁克家族“白人拉惹”的私人王国。1841年詹姆斯·布鲁克因协助平定叛乱，从文莱苏丹手中获得砂拉越；其继承者不断蚕食文莱领土，直到1946年查尔斯·维纳·布鲁克将其割让给英国王室。

sources.title: Steven Runciman, The White Rajahs: A History of Sarawak from 1841 to 1946 (Cambridge University Press, 1960)
Barbara Watson Andaya & Leonard Y. Andaya, A History of Malaysia (Palgrave, 3rd ed. 2017)
Wikipedia: Raj of Sarawak

note: Japan occupied Sarawak 1941–1945.

summary.en: The Indochinese Union of Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia, joined by Laos in 1893, ruled by a governor-general. It built railways, rubber plantations and a colonial Hanoi while suppressing nationalist revolts, and dissolved after the defeat at Điện Biên Phủ and the Geneva Accords.
summary.zh: 由交趾支那、安南、东京和柬埔寨组成的印度支那联邦，1893年加入老挝，由总督统治。殖民当局修建铁路、橡胶种植园和殖民地风格的河内，同时镇压民族主义起义；奠边府战败和日内瓦协议后解体。

sources.title: Pierre Brocheux & Daniel Hémery, Indochina: An Ambiguous Colonization, 1858–1954 (University of California Press, 2009)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: French Indochina
Wikipedia: French Indochina

note: Rulers listed are governors-general.

story.en:
France assembled Indochina piece by piece: Cochinchina by conquest in 1862–1867, Cambodia as a protectorate in 1863, Annam and Tonkin after the war with China in 1883–1885. In October 1887 these were joined as the Indochinese Union, and Laos was added after France forced Siam to give up the east bank of the Mekong in 1893.

The governor-general Paul Doumer (1897–1902), later president of France, gave the federation its machinery: state monopolies on opium, salt and alcohol, a budget that made the colony pay for itself, and the railway that would eventually link Hanoi with Saigon. Rubber plantations in the south became notorious for the death rates among contract labourers.

Colonial schools also produced the critics of colonialism. Phan Bội Châu, Nguyễn Ái Quốc (later Hồ Chí Minh) and the Yên Bái mutineers of 1930 all came out of this system. Japan occupied the colony from 1940, overthrew the French in March 1945, and the war that followed ended French Indochina at Điện Biên Phủ.
story.zh:
法国是一块块拼凑出印度支那的：1862—1867年征服交趾支那，1863年使柬埔寨成为保护国，1883—1885年中法战争后取得安南与东京。1887年10月，这些地区合组为印度支那联邦；1893年法国迫使暹罗放弃湄公河东岸后，老挝也被并入。

总督保罗·杜美（1897—1902年在任，后任法国总统）为联邦建立了统治机器：鸦片、盐和酒的官营专卖，让殖民地自负盈亏的预算，以及后来贯通河内与西贡的铁路。南方的橡胶园则因契约劳工的高死亡率而臭名昭著。

殖民学校也培养出了殖民主义的批判者，潘佩珠、阮爱国（即后来的胡志明）以及1930年安沛起义的士兵都出自这一体系。1940年日本进驻，1945年3月推翻法国当局，随后爆发的战争最终在奠边府终结了法属印度支那。

summary.en: The anti-communist state south of the 17th parallel, proclaimed by Ngô Đình Diệm after a rigged referendum deposed Bảo Đại. Dependent on American aid and troops, it was shaken by coups after Diệm's murder in 1963 and surrendered when North Vietnamese tanks entered Saigon on 30 April 1975.
summary.zh: 北纬17度线以南的反共国家，吴庭艳通过一场操纵的公投废黜保大后宣布成立。它依赖美国援助与驻军，1963年吴庭艳被杀后政变频仍，1975年4月30日北越坦克开进西贡时宣布投降。

sources.title: Fredrik Logevall, Embers of War (Random House, 2012)
Edward Miller, Misalliance: Ngo Dinh Diem, the United States, and the Fate of South Vietnam (Harvard University Press, 2013)
Wikipedia: South Vietnam

summary.en: The Khmer Rouge state, which emptied the cities, abolished money, markets and religion and drove the population into collective farms. Between 1.5 and 2 million people died of execution, starvation and disease before the Vietnamese invasion of January 1979 drove the regime to the Thai border.
summary.zh: 红色高棉建立的国家。它清空城市，废除货币、市场和宗教，把全体人民驱赶进集体农场。在1979年1月越南入侵、政权退往泰柬边境之前，约150万至200万人死于处决、饥饿和疾病。
